independent_computation.step_1: Locate the effect in cached source data. data/items.json id 3877 is Bloodsong; its only passive branch (S1) defines Expose Weakness as a 4-second debuff on champions.
independent_computation.step_2: Read the amplifier magnitude. The branch states the debuffed target takes {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES — i.e. it amplifies damage dealt by any ally, not only the Bloodsong holder. That matches a leaf named 'support_damage_multiplier' being applied to a combat event on another champion's damage timeline.
independent_computation.step_3: Resolve the {{rd|A|B}} template. Per S3 (repo's own corpus resolving Serpent's Fang {{rd|50%|35%}} to 50 % melee / 35 % ranged) and S4 (every other rd usage in items.json puts the melee value first), A = 8 % applies when the Bloodsong holder is melee, B = 5 % when ranged.
independent_computation.step_4: Convert the amplifier to a multiplier. 'Take X% increased damage' is a multiplicative outgoing-damage amp: multiplier = 1 + X/100.
independent_computation.arithmetic: 1 + 0.08 = 1.08 (exact; the 8.0 'percent' slot in S2 is the same figure the wiki text carries)

residual_uncertainty.statement: The melee-vs-ranged branch depends on which ally in the cleaver_bloodsong_roster holds Bloodsong. Roster composition is defined in scenario/test code, which this oracle is forbidden to read, so it could not be confirmed from data/.
residual_uncertainty.why_it_does_not_change_the_verdict: 1.08 reproduces the cached 8 % melee figure exactly and to the digit; the only competing candidate the source admits is 1.05 (ranged). The emitted leaf is therefore a faithful, unrounded read of a real current value in data/items.json rather than a stale or invented constant — nothing in the permitted evidence contradicts it.
residual_uncertainty.follow_up_for_the_change_author: Confirm the Bloodsong holder in this roster is melee. If that ally is a ranged champion, the correct leaf is {"multiplier": 1.05}; verify the implementation actually branches on the holder's attack type rather than hard-coding 8 %.
